lines.text: The Order did. With a draught. And Maric drank it, because he wanted to beat me.
My father didn't shout. He sat down on the other side of the bed, very slowly, like an old man. I had never once thought of him as old.
For a long time, neither of us said anything. Maric breathed. The sheets steamed. My father and I had never been good at beginnings.
Your wardship ended with the Tourney. Until the council meets, you belong to no one. That is three days.
There is a barge at the river gate, Lucan. Its captain is paid. Take your people north. Tonight.
They have Ilse. They have Maric's cure, locked under the cathedral. I'm not running.
You can't fight them. You can't fight anyone. You never could.
I've never fought anyone in my life. I've won anyway.
He looked at me then, really looked, the way he had in his tent at Senn Ford. As if I might be worth listening to.
There are things I should have told you, a long time ago. When you are safe, I will tell you all of them. I swear it.
Then I'll make sure I'm safe.
His eyes went to my collar, where the cord of his plain ring showed. The ring from a woman I never met. He looked away very quickly.
Maric woke just once, near midnight. His eyes were as white as candle wax.
Little brother. Go home. Builds character.
It was the first joke he had ever made with me, instead of at me. Then the fever took him back.
Before I left, I asked my father for one thing. To let Hobb sit with Maric through the nights.
A brickmaker? In my son's sickroom?
If Maric gets worse, Hobb will know. And if Hobb knows, I'll feel it. Wherever I am.
My father knew more than he ever said. I think he knew exactly what I meant. He let Hobb sit.
Hobb wouldn't touch the silk chairs. He sat on the floor by the bed with his sooty hands in his lap, and called my brother sir, even asleep.
On my way out, Ash stopped by my father's chair. My father patted his head, very stiffly, the way you'd pat a dog the size of a horse.
Then I walked down into the Lowmarket. No Holt, for once. Only Ash.
I had a bookkeeper, a hunter, a burned knight, a runaway Measurer, and sixty brickmakers. And three nights to break into the most guarded place in Aldmere.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter ninety-three, coming soon.
